name: Angel food cake
origin: A 19th-century American invention that used up the many egg whites left over from other kitchen work (custards, mayonnaise); it is the leanest of the classic American foam cakes, with no fat and no egg yolk at all.

ingredients.note: egg white only; the defining absence of any yolk (and so any fat) is what gives angel food its distinctively light, pure-white crumb

process.name: whip whites
process.description: whip egg whites (with cream of tartar as a whipping stabiliser, negligible mass) to soft peaks

process.name: add sugar
process.description: add half the sugar gradually, whipping to stiff, glossy peaks

process.name: fold in flour and sugar
process.description: sift the remaining sugar with the flour and fold into the meringue in stages

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in an ungreased tube pan (the ungreased sides let the foam climb and cling as it sets), then cool inverted

notes: Egg white around 200-250% of flour mass and no fat at all is the real, defining ratio of angel food (Gisslen, Professional Baking, foam-cake method). No chemical leavening: aeration is entirely the whipped egg-white foam, so leavening-role mass is correctly zero here rather than omitted by oversight. structureIndex is strongly positive (no sugar/fat tenderiser mass to offset flour+egg), matching angel food's real reputation as the driest, most tightly-set of the classic American cakes.
